eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in official forecasts from the China Meteorological Administration, which project a 29°C high for Guangzhou on May 11 amid thundershowers and high humidity, closely matching the 31.5% implied probability for 29°C and 36% for 30°C. Persistent overcast conditions today, capping temperatures at 23–27°C per Guangzhou Central Meteorological Observatory, signal ongoing convective activity from the region's early monsoon influences, suppressing peak solar heating while urban heat island effects and variable cloud breaks could nudge readings toward 30°C. Model consensus shows slight divergence, with BBC and WMO aligning at 29°C; evening updates from CMA and global ensembles like GFS/ECMWF may clarify timing of showers critical to final outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in short-range forecasts from the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD), with implied probabilities clustered around 35°C (31%) and 36°C (29.5%) for Karachi's highest temperature on May 12 amid an ongoing pre-monsoon heatwave. PMD's latest weekly outlook for May 6-12 projects warm, very humid conditions in Sindh, with fast sea breezes at 25-50 km/h moderating peaks through cooler marine air advection and evaporative cooling, while continental high pressure builds heat. Differentiating factors include sea breeze timing—early arrival caps at 35°C, delays allow 36-37°C—and potential dust storms May 11-13 reducing solar insolation. Global models like ECMWF show ensemble spread of 1-2°C; watch PMD's May 11 daily update for refinement before resolution via official airport observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's extended weather outlook, issued May 10, forecasts Metro Manila highs of 31–35°C on May 12 under easterlies with partly cloudy skies and isolated rainshowers, driving trader consensus toward 37°C (39%) and 36°C (30%) as leading outcomes amid close competition. Persistent dry season subsidence and urban heat island effects in central Manila, including Quezon City observatory readings, elevate implied probabilities above baseline May averages of 33–34°C, while low rain chances (20–40%) limit cooling. ENSO-neutral conditions prevail, but potential early El Niño signals could amplify heat; key differentiators include sea breeze timing and thunderstorm coverage, with new PAGASA bulletins expected daily resolving uncertainties before the 24-hour observation window.
